segments.context: Image: Blue Bottle Coffee. Blue Bottle Coffee US image of the 12 oz whole-bean package; packaging is not a current-lot certificate.

segments.source: 17ft Ceiling is the distinct Blue Bottle dark espresso for a buyer who wants a classic short-shot direction and is comfortable with a named robusta accent. Blue Bottle says its Latin American and East African coffees and fine robusta serve body and crema. Those are formulation and roaster-positioning claims, not Coffeedant extraction measurements.

segments.source: Bella Donovan makes sense when a dark daily drip coffee should retain a roaster-described berry edge under chocolate and molasses. Blue Bottle attributes that fruit to a natural-processed Ethiopian component and explicitly invites milk or cream. The full current blend recipe and delivered roast date still need a bag check.

segments.source: Giant Steps has one unusually useful piece of product-specific brew guidance: Blue Bottle labels it for French press with milk and gives a 1:13 ratio. It is a defensible first bag for someone who wants a developed chocolate direction in a press, with the caveat that roaster notes and an older independent cup cannot predict today’s delivered bag.

segments.source: Hayes Valley is the clearest Blue Bottle first bag for someone recreating its chocolate-led café espresso or a small milk drink. The US page names washed processing, dark roasting and short ristretto service. Its tasting words and café practice do not prove how a home machine will extract a particular bag.

segments.source: Night Light Decaf is a useful one-bag trial for a US household moving between decaf espresso and French press. Blue Bottle says it uses a water decaffeination process and positions the coffee for both black and milk drinks. The US page’s medium label and darker flavor description should be read together; neither establishes a Coffeedant tasting or residual-caffeine measurement.
